simple.meaning: בָּזַר (bâzar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to disperse.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Psalms, Daniel, beginning at Psalms 68:31. The surrounding contexts include family, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּזַר (H967) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּזַר (bâzar) / H967 is traced through Psalms 68:31, Daniel 11:24 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H967. bazar [ בָּזַר ] verb scatter (Arabic , Aramaic בְּדַר ) — Qal Imperfect Dan 11:24 יִבְז֑וֺר לָהֶם וּרְכוּשׁ וְשָׁלָל בִּזָּה plunder and spoil and possessions he will scatter among them (subject Antiochus Epiph.) Pi`el Perfect בִּזַּר , id. , Psa 68:31 , but read Imperative בַּזֵּר (בַּזַּר) ( ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 so most; De follows MT), subject reference to ׳י , object עַמִּים .

occurrences.englishText: Princes shall come out of Egypt.

In time of security he will come even on the fattest places of the province. He will do that which his fathers have not done, nor his fathers’ fathers. He will scatter among them prey, plunder, and substance. Yes, he will devise his plans against the strongholds, even for a time.
